subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled: false` be a hard read/exec access boundary for the skill directory, or should disabled skills remain eligibility-only while a separate capability/filesystem policy owns hard access control?
rationale: The answer changes the security meaning of an existing public toggle and affects prompt exposure, read/write/apply_patch, exec, sandbox behavior, Gateway/UI status, and docs, so automation cannot safely choose it.

options.title: Define a hard disabled-skill boundary
options.body: Treat disabled skill directories as centrally denied roots and make exec either deny those paths, run under isolation that enforces them, or clearly disable exec for that guarantee.

options.title: Keep enabled as eligibility-only
options.body: Document and rename the UI/config semantics so operators know hard access control must be handled by tool policy, sandboxing, or filesystem roots.

options.title: Fold into capability policy
options.body: Canonicalize this under the broader skill/tool capability model and keep #57119 linked as the disabled-toggle acceptance case.

recommendation.title: Define a hard disabled-skill boundary
recommendation.body: Treat disabled skill directories as centrally denied roots and make exec either deny those paths, run under isolation that enforces them, or clearly disable exec for that guarantee.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a security/product boundary choice, and recent history shows adjacent security direction and agent/tool policy work rather than a narrow single-file owner.
